title: Fate of Existing Overrides at or After the Split Point on a THIS_AND_FUTURE Edit
question: When a THIS_AND_FUTURE edit splits a series at split_rid, what happens to existing single-instance overrides whose RECURRENCE-ID is at or after split_rid?
spec_gap: RFC 5545 states that a RANGE=THISANDFUTURE change does not impact subsequent instances defined in separate components, while RFC 8984 Section 4.1.3 requires splitting into a new recurring object with a new UID without specifying whether per-instance overrides at or after the split point are discarded or migrated to the new series. A THIS_AND_FUTURE delete clearly removes them; for an edit, an override's RECURRENCE-ID may still match a candidate occurrence of the new future segment.

citations.verbatim_quote: Subsequent instances are determined by their "RECURRENCE-ID" value and not their current scheduled start time. Subsequent instances defined in separate components are not impacted by the given recurrence instance.

options.summary: Standalone overrides with RECURRENCE-ID >= split_rid are removed; the new future segment starts with no exceptions.
consequences: Simple, and identical to the THIS_AND_FUTURE delete behavior.
Per-instance edits after the split point are silently lost.

options.summary: Standalone overrides with RECURRENCE-ID >= split_rid whose RECURRENCE-ID instant is a candidate occurrence of the new future segment are kept and re-keyed to the new segment's UID (with RECURRENCE-ID unchanged in instant); overrides that are not candidates of the new segment (for example, when the split edit shifted DTSTART) are removed.
consequences: Preserves per-instance edits after the split point whenever the recurrence slots still align.
When the split edit shifts DTSTART to a different time of day or changes the RRULE pattern so an override's RECURRENCE-ID is no longer a candidate of the new segment, that override is discarded.
